title: Difficulty spreads in lessons, not exam sets
statement: Across a lesson, the questions on one source should range from easier to harder without strict ordering, while an exam-style set on one source keeps them at one level.
example: One rubric expects uniform difficulty across a set of 3-5 questions sharing a single stimulus, as standardized tests do.
detail: The evaluator's lesson rubric, for one passage with a mixed set of questions, passes a lesson whose questions run from recall to inference and synthesis and fails one where all cluster at one level, without requiring strict easy-to-hard order (`shadow/bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/lesson_bundle/evaluation.txt` lines 95-97). Its rubric for a small set of questions sharing one stimulus expects uniform difficulty instead, unlike a quiz, to match standardized test formats (`mcq_set/evaluation.txt` line 3), and the AP chemistry overlay says the same of stimulus-based sets (`question/ap_chemistry_evaluation.txt` lines 55-57). Both are adopted rules; neither has been measured on learners.

evidence.quote: Pass: questions span a range from easier (recall/retrieval) to harder (inference/synthesis), appropriate for the grade level. Perfect E→M→H ordering is NOT required.
Unlike quizzes which require Easy/Medium/Hard distribution, MCQ sets are expected to have UNIFORM difficulty - all questions should be at the same appropriate difficulty level.
uniform (not escalating) difficulty across the set is expected.
